newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end listless session lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end listless session lower.

text.p: *Stocks ended slightly lower in listless trade after weak leads from offshore markets. Volume 266.7 million shares, value A$411.8 million, 1,043 stocks traded, 331 steady, 357 up, 355 down.
Australian shares closed slightly lower after a listless session of trade on Monday as investors were left uninspired by weak leads from offshore markets and a lack of local news to drive the market.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed four points lower at 2,358.1, off its intra-day of 2,366.1.
The December share price index ended down six points at 2,367, an 8.9 point premium to the underlying index.
At a little over A$400 million, the day's turnover was about half the daily average in the past few months and highlighted the lack of interest in the market.

"A holiday on Wall Street tonight meant there were quite a few people not prepared to show their hand today because they could step into quite a different market a couple of days from now," said Paul Ford, a dealer at Sydney firm Shaw Stockbroking.
Ford said the market's main feature was the lack of buying interest. "A lot of investors are hesistant to buy until the market gives a better indication of its near-term direction," he said.
Both the industrial and resource sectors finished lower, although the resource sector would have ended lower except for the resilient performance of some metal miners.

The shares of building products and sugar group CSR were active and weaker after the company reported lower half year results and signalled that its second half was likely to be considerably down on the previous year.
In other markets, Australian bonds churned in a narrow range during a listless trading session in the absence of major data and due to today's U.S. Veteran's Day holiday.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds finished at 7.20 percent, down 0.01 percentage point from their closing level on Friday.
The Australian dollar spent the U.S. holiday-hit Monday session consolidating an offshore rally, but lacked the momentum to extend the bounce to safe territory.
At 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), the currency was quoted at US$0.7875/80.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Both options and futures trade was very subdued, reflecting the low turnover in the physical market.
Total options traded 30,872 (38,139)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 1,403 (4,152)

Building products and sugar group's shares ended lower after it said its half year net profit fell 24 pct to A$154.7 million and expected its second half result to be much weaker than last year *Burns Philp A$1.95 (unch) 1.94/1.96 Vol: 386,351 Food ingredients group said it saw better earnings in 1996/97.

*McIntosh last trade A$1.25 on Friday (+.15) Trading in broking house's shares halted, pending announcement following rumour the company was likely the subject of a takeover offer by U.S. securities house Merrill Lynch.
Big resources ended weaker on softer copper/aluminium prices.
Construction group's shares ended up after a positive review in a Saturday newspaper.
